name: mon16-6
why: A bold false claim, a one-vote upset, and a killer’s parting lie make the final blunder entertaining despite some repeated arguments.

moments.text: Opus uses his certain reveal to plant the lie that wins for Gemma.
The town votes out its real officer by a single vote.
Haiku catches Terra contradicting himself, making the wrong choice feel earned.

dull.why: The confirmed officer’s read is repeated several times before the inevitable Opus vote.

irony.evidence: I'm the officer. I was shown Sonnet.

reversal.evidence: VOTE: Sonnet 4 (Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Opus); Opus 3 (Sonnet, Luna, Terra)

mistake.evidence: I protected Gemma, so Sol’s death clears her; Haiku is twisting it.

voices.evidence: That's a confession, not a defense.

clash.evidence: I'm the officer. I was shown Opus as the killer, not the other way around.

freshness.evidence: Sonnet’s revealed card makes your claim collapse; I’m not moving off you.

ending.evidence: My partner is Terra — he buried me hardest to look clean.
